## Model comparison (M0 = no time effect, M1 = with time effect)

**Headline result -- report this pair.** From
`loo_compare()` in `kim_analysis_stddm.R` (saved to
`model_comparison_indices.RData`):

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| elpd_diff (M0 vs M1) | -137.60 |
| se_diff | 18.15 |

`elpd_diff` and `se_diff` are on the **elpd** scale. The absolute WAIC/LOOIC
below are on the **-2 x elpd** scale; do not place `se_diff` next to a
difference of those. Do not report the absolute SEs (~350) as the uncertainty
of the comparison: they describe variability of each model's total across all
trials, whereas `se_diff` comes from the pointwise elpd contrasts on the same
observations, where the two models' errors are highly correlated.

This is **trial-level** LOO (`ld_comp` is per-trial), i.e. held-out trial
prediction, not leave-one-participant-out.

M1 is favoured by **7.6 standard errors** (137.60 / 18.15), so the comparison
is decisive rather than marginal.

**Pareto k diagnostics:** 262 / 25,975 trials (1.0%) exceed k = 0.7 under M0
and 269 / 25,975 (1.1%) under M1. The counts are near-identical across models,
so the induced bias largely cancels in the difference, and 262 unreliable
points cannot move a 7.6-SE gap. PSIS-LOO is reliable here.

Note that WAIC flagged far *more* problem observations than PSIS-LOO did
(1,885 trials, 7.3%, with p_waic > 0.4 under M0; 1,855, 7.1%, under M1).
WAIC is therefore not a safer fallback than LOO on these data -- it degrades
harder on the same trials. LOO is the primary index; WAIC and DIC are
secondary.

**Absolute values (secondary; SEs are of each total, not of the difference):**

| model | DIC | WAIC (SE) | LOOIC (SE) |
|---|---|---|---|
| M0 (no time effect) | 51833.97 | 55526.92 (351.70) | 56106.64 (357.57) |
| M1 (with time effect) | 51644.23 | 55261.85 (354.88) | 55831.44 (360.99) |

DIC here is the hand-computed variant in `calculate_indices()` using
`D_hat = min(deviance)`, which is chain-length dependent -- treat it as the
weakest of the three.

```{r}
# Data preprocessing
risk_data <- risk_data %>%
  mutate(
    rt = rt / 1000, # Convert reaction time to seconds
    response = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0),
    RT = if_else(response == 0, -rt, rt), # Negative RT for 'No' responses
    risk = risk * 0.01, # Convert percentages to proportions
    gain = gain * 0.01,
    no_effect = no_effect * 0.01,
    idxP = as.numeric(as.factor(user_id)) # Create numeric subject index
  ) 

# m0_predictions / m1_predictions have one row per RAW trial (25975), in the same

# subset identically downstream (see the Figure 2 chunk); filtering risk_data alone
# leaves it at 25563 rows and misaligns it against the 25975-row prediction matrices.
keep_rows <- risk_data$idxP %in% unique_idxP_table$idxP
risk_data <- risk_data %>%
  filter(keep_rows)
```

# Figure 1 (PPC)

```{r}
create_ppc_plot <- function(predictions, observed_data, model_name) {
  predicted_data <- tibble(
    RT = as.vector(predictions),
    draw = rep(1:ncol(predictions), each = nrow(predictions))
  )

  ggplot() +
  # Predicted (average) - red line for predicted
  stat_density(
    data = predicted_data, aes(x = abs(RT), color = "Predicted"),
    geom = "line", position = "identity", linewidth = 1, linetype = "solid"
  ) +
  # Observed - black line for observed
  stat_density(
    data = observed_data, aes(x = abs(RT), color = "Observed"),
    geom = "line", position = "identity", linewidth = 1, linetype = "solid"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Posterior Predictive Check:", model_name),
    x = "Response Time (seconds)",
    y = "Density",
    color = "Legend"  # Label for the legend
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Predicted" = "red", "Observed" = "black")) +  # Define colors in the legend
  theme_tidybayes() +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 24),  # Increase font size for axis labels
    axis.text = element_text(size = 18),    # Adjust tick label size
    plot.title = element_text(size = 24, face = "bold", family = "serif"),  # Increase title font size
    text = element_text(family = "serif"),  # Set the overall plot font to serif
    legend.position = "right",  # Position the legend to the right (can change to "top", "bottom", etc.)
    legend.box = "box",  # Put the legend inside a box
    legend.background = element_rect(color = "black"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 18),  # Increase the legend text size
    legend.title =  element_blank()
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 7.5)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 2.0))

 
}


```

```{r}
m0_ppc_plot <- create_ppc_plot(m0_predictions, observed_data, "M0 (without time effect)")
m1_ppc_plot <- create_ppc_plot(m1_predictions, observed_data, "M1 (with time effect)")
print(m0_ppc_plot)
print(m1_ppc_plot)
```

```{r}
# Assuming m0_ppc_plot and m1_ppc_plot are your existing plots

  theme = theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 32, face = "bold", family="serif", hjust = 0.5)  # Set the size and style of the main title
  )
)

```

# Figure 2 (Gain and Risk Predictions)

```{r}
# Create a comparison plot with overlaid data
create_comparison_plot_rt <- function(observed_data, predicted_data, x_var, y_var, x_label, y_label, y_limits = NULL, convert_predicted_to_seconds = FALSE) {
  observed_summary <- observed_data %>%
    mutate({{ x_var }} := {{ x_var }} * 100) %>%
    group_by({{ x_var }}, experimental_treatment_selected) %>%
    summarise(
      m_left = mean({{ y_var }}),
      se = sqrt(var({{ y_var }}) / n()),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  predicted_summary <- predicted_data %>%
    mutate({{ x_var }} := {{ x_var }} * 100) %>%
    group_by({{ x_var }}, experimental_treatment_selected) %>%
    summarise(
      m_left = if (convert_predicted_to_seconds) mean({{ y_var }}) / 1000 else mean({{ y_var }}),
      se = if (convert_predicted_to_seconds) sqrt(var({{ y_var }})) / (1000 * sqrt(n())) else sqrt(var({{ y_var }}) / n()),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  plot <- ggplot() +
    geom_pointrange(
      data = observed_summary,
      aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left, ymin = m_left - 1.96 * se, ymax = m_left + 1.96 * se, color = "Observed", shape = experimental_treatment_selected)
    ) +
    geom_line(data = observed_summary, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left, color = "Observed", shape = experimental_treatment_selected, linetype = experimental_treatment_selected), size = 0.6) +
    geom_pointrange(
      data = predicted_summary,
      aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left, ymin = m_left - 1.96 * se, ymax = m_left + 1.96 * se, color = "Predicted", shape = experimental_treatment_selected)
    ) +
    geom_line(data = predicted_summary, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left, color = "Predicted", shape = experimental_treatment_selected, linetype = experimental_treatment_selected), size = 0.6) +
    theme_classic() +
    geom_smooth(data=observed_summary, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left), method="lm") +
    geom_smooth(data=predicted_summary, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left), method="lm") +
    # geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed", size = .2) +
    labs(y = y_label, x = x_label, color = "Data") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Observed" = "blue", "Predicted" = "red")) +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 15), legend.position = "bottom")

  if (!is.null(y_limits)) {
    plot <- plot + scale_y_continuous(limits = y_limits)
  }

  return(plot)
}

# Create a comparison plot with overlaid data
create_comparison_plot_choice <- function(observed_data, predicted_data, x_var, y_var, x_label, y_label, y_limits = NULL, convert_predicted_to_seconds = FALSE) {
  observed_summary <- observed_data %>%
    mutate({{ x_var }} := {{ x_var }} * 100) %>%
    group_by({{ x_var }}) %>%
    summarise(
      m_left = mean({{ y_var }}),
      se = sqrt(var({{ y_var }}) / n()),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  predicted_summary <- predicted_data %>%
    mutate({{ x_var }} := {{ x_var }} * 100) %>%
    group_by({{ x_var }}) %>%
    summarise(
      m_left = if (convert_predicted_to_seconds) mean({{ y_var }}) / 1000 else mean({{ y_var }}),
      se = if (convert_predicted_to_seconds) sqrt(var({{ y_var }})) / (1000 * sqrt(n())) else sqrt(var({{ y_var }}) / n()),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  plot <- ggplot() +
    geom_pointrange(
      data = observed_summary,
      aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left, ymin = m_left - 1.96 * se, ymax = m_left + 1.96 * se, color = "Observed")
    ) +
    geom_line(data = observed_summary, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left, color = "Observed"), size = 0.6) +
    geom_pointrange(
      data = predicted_summary,
      aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left, ymin = m_left - 1.96 * se, ymax = m_left + 1.96 * se, color = "Predicted")
    ) +
    geom_line(data = predicted_summary, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left, color = "Predicted"), size = 0.6) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_text(size = 24),  # Increase font size for axis labels
      axis.title.y = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 18),    # Adjust tick label size
      plot.title = element_text(size = 24, face = "bold", family = "serif"),  # Increase title font size
      text = element_text(family = "serif"),  # Set the overall plot font to serif
      legend.position = "bottom",  # Position the legend to the right (can change to "top", "bottom", etc.)
      legend.box = "box",  # Put the legend inside a box
      legend.background = element_rect(color = "black"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 18),  # Increase the legend text size
      legend.title =  element_blank()
    ) +
    
    # geom_smooth(data=observed_summary, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left), method="lm") +
    # geom_smooth(data=predicted_summary, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = m_left), method="lm") +
    # geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed", size = .2) +
    labs(y = y_label, x = x_label, color = "Data") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Observed" = "blue", "Predicted" = "red")) +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 15), legend.position = "bottom")
  
  if (!is.null(y_limits)) {
    plot <- plot + scale_y_continuous(limits = y_limits)
  }
  
  return(plot)
}
```

# Figure 3 (DDM Heatmap)

## T Values

I'm using T values instead of beta coefficients, since these are standardized

```{r}
# `results` and `subscore_results` are not saved anywhere usable: they are built by
# DDM_STDDM_Regression.Rmd (the regression chunks near the end) and the .RData on
# disk predates the T_Value column. Run that notebook's save chunk once to create
# this file, then this load makes Figure 3 reproducible from a clean session.
load('regression_results_for_figures.RData')

# Create a wide format of the results data for t values
t_wide <- dcast(results, Independent_Var ~ Dependent_Var, value.var = "T_Value")

# Melt the wide data for ggplot2
t_melt <- melt(t_wide, id.vars = "Independent_Var", variable.name = "Dependent_Var", value.name = "t")

# Plot the heatmap for t values
fig_3_plot_t = ggplot(t_melt, aes(x = Dependent_Var, y = Independent_Var, fill = t)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white", midpoint = 0, 
                       limit = c(min(t_melt$t, na.rm=TRUE), max(t_melt$t, na.rm=TRUE)), name = "t-value") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 24, base_family = "serif") +
  theme(
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA), # White background for the panel
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),  # White background for the plot
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),  # Remove major gridlines
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),  # Remove minor gridlines
        # legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", size = 0.5),  # Add black border around legend
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),  # Bold legend title
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12)  # Adjust legend text size
        ) +  # Center and bold title
  labs(title = "Heatmap of t-values", x = "Drift Rate Parameters", y = "Ideological Variables")

print(fig_3_plot_t)

# Optionally, save the plot with increased width
ggsave("Figures/Fig3_HEATMAP_t.png", fig_3_plot_t, width = 16, height = 12)
```
## P Values

```{r}
# Ensure you have the necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

# Create a wide format of the results data for P_Value values
pvalue_wide <- dcast(results, Independent_Var ~ Dependent_Var, value.var = "P_Value")

# Melt the wide data for ggplot2
pvalue_melt <- melt(pvalue_wide, id.vars = "Independent_Var", variable.name = "Dependent_Var", value.name = "P_Value")

# Log transform the P-Values (adding a small value to avoid log(0) issues)
pvalue_melt$log_P_Value <- -log10(pvalue_melt$P_Value + 1e-10)

# Plot the heatmap for P_Value values (log-transformed)
fig_3_plot_pval = ggplot(pvalue_melt, aes(x = Dependent_Var, y = Independent_Var, fill = log_P_Value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "darkgreen", 
                      name = "Log(P-Value)", na.value = "grey50") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 24, base_family = "serif") +
  theme(
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA), # White background for the panel
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),  # White background for the plot
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),  # Remove major gridlines
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),  # Remove minor gridlines
        # legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", size = 0.5),  # Add black border around legend
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),  # Bold legend title
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12)  # Adjust legend text size
        ) +  # Center and bold title
  labs(title = "Heatmap of Log-Transformed P-Values", x = "Drift Rate Parameters", y = "Ideological Variables")

# Optionally, save the plot with increased width
ggsave("Figures/Fig3_HEATMAP_PVAL.png", fig_3_plot_pval, width = 16, height = 12)
```

# Figure 4 (Time varying graph)

Make each participant be a point on the graph. Use the average of the number of times that experimental treatment was selected as the y-axis

## Compute average of DDM Statistics

```{r}
# Step 1: Identify columns with square brackets in m1_posterior
# Extract columns that match the pattern with ".p[XX]" or just "[XX]"
selected_columns <- m1_posterior %>%
  select(matches("\\[\\d+\\]$"))

# Step 2: Calculate the averages for each column
averages <- selected_columns %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean, na.rm = TRUE))

# Step 3: Extract both metric_name and participant_id, handling both ".p[XX]" and "[XX]"
column_info <- tibble(
  full_colname = colnames(averages),
  participant_id = str_extract(colnames(averages), "(?<=\\[)\\d+(?=\\])"),  # Extract participant ID if present in square brackets
  metric_name = str_replace(colnames(averages), "\\.?p?\\[\\d+\\]$", "")  # Remove either ".p[XX]" or "[XX]"
)

# Pivot the data into wide format where each metric_name becomes a separate column
averages_wide <- averages %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "full_colname", values_to = "average") %>%
  left_join(column_info, by = "full_colname") %>%
  mutate(participant_id = as.numeric(participant_id)) %>%
  select(participant_id, metric_name, average) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric_name, values_from = average)  # Pivot into wide format
```

## Compute average response per participant then join

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Step 1: Group risk_data by idxP and calculate the average of the response column
risk_data_avg <- risk_data %>%
  group_by(idxP) %>%
  summarise(avg_response = mean(response, na.rm = TRUE))

# Step 2: Join the risk_data_avg with averages_wide by idxP and participant_id
participant_average <- risk_data_avg %>%
  left_join(averages_wide, by = c("
idxP" = "participant_id"))

# Step 3: (Optional) View the final data
head(participant_average)
```

## Plot response by time latency

Positive time parameter means risk comes first.
Negative time parameter means benefit comes first.

### Benefit

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

participant_average <- risk_data_avg %>%
  left_join(averages_wide, by = c("idxP" = "participant_id"))

# participant_average$b_diff <- abs(participant_average$b_gain - participant_average$b_risk)
# participant_average$b_diff <- participant_average$b_risk
participant_average$b_diff <- participant_average$b_gain

# Step 1: Split participant_average into 5 quintiles based on b_diff
participant_average <- participant_average %>%
  mutate(b_diff_group = cut(b_diff, breaks = quantile(b_diff, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2), na.rm = TRUE), include.lowest = TRUE))

# Step 2: For each b_gain group, split into 5 time quintiles and label them (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th)
participant_average <- participant_average %>%
  group_by(b_diff_group) %>%
  mutate(time_group = cut(time, breaks = quantile(time, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2), na.rm = TRUE), 
                          labels = c("1st \n(Cure earlier)", "2nd", "3rd", "4th", "5th \n(Harm earlier)"), include.lowest = TRUE))


# Step 3: Calculate the average and confidence intervals for avg_response in each b_gain and time quintile
summary_data <- participant_average %>%
  group_by(b_diff_group, time_group) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_response_mean = mean(avg_response, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_response_ci_lower = mean(avg_response, na.rm = TRUE) - 1.96 * sd(avg_response, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    avg_response_ci_upper = mean(avg_response, na.rm = TRUE) + 1.96 * sd(avg_response, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())
  )

# Step 4: Plot all b_gain groups on the same plot with time quintiles on x-axis
fig4_plot <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = time_group, y = avg_response_mean, color = b_diff_group, group = b_diff_group)) +
  geom_line(size = 3) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = avg_response_ci_lower, ymax = avg_response_ci_upper), width = 0.1) +  # Add error bars
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 2) +  # Add dashed vertical line for zero
  labs(x = "Relative Onset Quintiles",color = "Cure Sensitivity") +
  ggtitle("Grouped by Cure Sensitivity") +  # Add title
  theme_minimal(base_family = "arial") +  # Change font to serif
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 84, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),  # Increase title font size
    axis.title = element_text(size = 72, face = "bold"),  # Increase axis label font size
    axis.text = element_text(size = 72),   # Increase axis text size
    legend.text = element_text(size = 72), # Increase legend text size
    legend.title = element_text(size = 72, face = "bold"), # Increase legend title size
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "white"),  # White panel background
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "white"),   # White plot background
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80"),   # Optional: Adjust grid lines for better visibility
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey90"),    # Optional: Lighter minor grid lines
    # axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 20), face = "bold")
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 40), face = "bold"),  # Add space between x-axis title and text
  ) + 
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("#0000FF", "#007FFF", "green", "#FF7F7F", "#FF0000"),  # Adjust colors as needed
    # labels = c("Smallest difference", "", "", "", "Biggest difference"),  # Custom legend labels
        labels = c("Least sensitive", "", "", "", "Most sensitive"),  # Custom legend labels
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5))  # Increase legend icon size
  ) + 
  ylim(0, 1)

print(fig4_plot)

# Optionally, save the plot with increased width
ggsave("Figures/Fig4_TIME_LATENCY_BENEFIT.png", fig4_plot, width = 24, height = 16)
```

## Large Factor Labels

> Defines the 12 overarching categories and the hand-picked palette used by the
> published figures. Run this chunk, then 'Draw Plot'. Do NOT also run
> 'Factor Cluster Labels' below -- it overwrites all three objects defined here.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
# importance_results for the item-level plots; written by DDM_STDDM_Regression.Rmd.
# Loaded into its own environment so final_table etc. in this session are not overwritten.
ridge_env <- new.env()
load("ridge_inputs.RData", envir = ridge_env)
importance_results <- ridge_env$importance_results
category_colors <- c(
  "BIG5" = "#808080",
  "Moral Foundations (MFQ)" = "#009E73",
  "Religious & Spiritual" = "#F0E442", 
  "Risk Taking (GRiPS)" = "#d62728",
  "Interpersonal Reactivity" = "#88CCEE",
  "Values (Schwartz)" = "#AA4499",
  "Political" = "#117733",
  "Demographics" = "#882255",
  "Moral Commitments" = "#bcbd22",
  "Numeracy" = "#661100",
  "Optimize" = "#332288",
  "Human Mind" = "#D55E00"
  # "Other" = "#7f7f7f"
)

# Update category mapping to separate BIG5 dimensions based on scoring key
category_mapping <- list(
  "BIG5" = "^BIG5",
  
  # Rest of categories remain the same
  "Moral Foundations (MFQ)" = "^MFSQ",
  "Religious & Spiritual" = c("^Religion", "^AttendChurch", "Spirituality", "Religiosity", "^ReligiousActivity", "meditation"),
  "Risk Taking (GRiPS)" = "^GRiPS_",
  "Interpersonal Reactivity" = c("^PT", "^EC", "^PD", "^FS"),
  "Values (Schwartz)" = c("TRADITION", "SELF.DIRECTION", "SECURITY", "CONFORMITY", "BENEVOLENCE",
                          "POWER", "ACHIEVEMENT", "STIMULATION", "HEDONISM", "UNIVERSALISM"),
  "Political" = c("^Political_Party", "liberal", "conservative", "republican", "democrat", "independent"),
  "Demographics" = c("^education", "^RelationshipStatus", "age", "^sex", "race_ethnicity", "YearOfEducation"),
  "Moral Commitments" = "^MC_",
  "Numeracy" = c("^Berlin", "^SNS"),
  "Optimize" = "Optimize",
  "Human Mind" = "HumanMind"
)

# Define parameter names with expressions for rendering
measure_names <- c(
  "time" = expression(s[time]),
  "b_gain" = expression(nu[beta[gain]]),
  "b_risk" = expression(nu[beta[risk]]),
  "alpha" = expression(alpha),
  "theta" = expression(tau),
  "bias" = expression(z)
)

# Function to map to the categories we hard-coded above
get_category <- function(feature_name) {
  for(cat_name in names(category_mapping)) {
    patterns <- category_mapping[[cat_name]]
    # Bare item names ("BIG5_1", "MFSQ1") must match exactly; unanchored, "BIG5_1" also matches BIG5_10-19
    patterns <- ifelse(grepl("^[A-Za-z0-9_]+[0-9]$", patterns), paste0("^", patterns, "$"), patterns)
    if(any(sapply(patterns, function(p) grepl(p, feature_name)))) {
      return(cat_name)
    }
  }
  return("Other")
}
```

```{r}
# Define parameter names with expressions for rendering
measure_names <- c(
  "time" = expression(s[time]),
  "b_gain" = expression(nu[beta[gain]]),
  "b_risk" = expression(nu[beta[risk]]),
  "alpha" = expression(alpha),
  "theta" = expression(tau),
  "bias" = expression(z)
)

# Function to map to the categories we hard-coded above
get_category <- function(feature_name) {
  for(cat_name in names(category_mapping)) {
    patterns <- category_mapping[[cat_name]]
    # Bare item names ("BIG5_1", "MFSQ1") must match exactly; unanchored, "BIG5_1" also matches BIG5_10-19
    patterns <- ifelse(grepl("^[A-Za-z0-9_]+[0-9]$", patterns), paste0("^", patterns, "$"), patterns)
    if(any(sapply(patterns, function(p) grepl(p, feature_name)))) {
      return(cat_name)
    }
  }
  return("Other")
}

library(grDevices)

# `categories` is the vector of category labels the palette is built over; it is the
# names of category_mapping, which it was renamed from.
categories <- names(category_mapping)

# Define a custom jet-like color palette
jet_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "cyan", "yellow", "red"))(length(categories))

# Assign colors to categories
category_colors <- setNames(jet_colors, categories)
```

## Draw Plot
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

measure_names <- c(

)

# Short descriptions for the inset items (text from data/text_key.csv). BFI-2 domain in
# parentheses: O, C, E, A, N (negative emotionality); "rev." = reverse-keyed item.
# Berlin dummies (e.g. Berlin31) = that problem answered correctly. Items not listed
# here keep their code, so a change in the top 10 shows up as a raw code.
item_labels <- c(
  "Berlin11"       = "Choir problem (correct)",
  "Berlin21"       = "Five-sided die (correct)",
  "Berlin31"       = "Loaded die (correct)",
  "SNS6"           = "Prefers numbers to words",

  "MFSQ18"         = "Laws should treat all fairly",

create_importance_plot <- function(data, measure) {

  data_plt <- data %>%
    mutate(
      Category = sapply(Feature, get_category),
      Label = ifelse(Feature %in% names(item_labels), item_labels[Feature], Feature),
      StdError = StdError,
      Importance = Importance
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(Importance))
  
  # Get top 10 data for inset
  top_10_data <- data_plt %>%
    slice(1:10)
  
  data_plt$Category <- factor(data_plt$Category, levels = names(category_colors))
  # browser()
  # main plot
  main_plot <- ggplot(data_plt, 
                      aes(x = Importance, 
                          y = reorder(Feature, Importance),
                          fill = Category)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = category_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = scales::scientific_format(digits = 2),
      breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 6),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
 plot.title = element_markdown(
    family = "Arial", size = 64, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 5)
  ),
  text = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 24),
  axis.title = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 56, face = "bold"),
  axis.text = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 32),
  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
  legend.title = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 56, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 56),
  legend.position = "right",
  legend.key.size = unit(1.5, "cm"),
  axis.text.y = element_blank(),
  axis.line.y = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks = element_blank(),
  panel.grid = element_blank(),
  plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20, unit = "pt")
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Feature Importance",
      y = "Items",
      fill = "Surveys",
      title = measure_names[measure]
    )
  
  # inset plot
  main_plot + 
    annotation_custom(
      ggplotGrob(
        ggplot(top_10_data,
               aes(x = Importance,
                   y = reorder(Label, Importance),
                   fill = Category)) +
          geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
          scale_fill_manual(values = category_colors, drop = FALSE) +
          scale_x_continuous(
            labels = scales::scientific_format(digits = 2),
            breaks = function(x) c(min(x), max(x))
          ) +
          theme_classic() +
          theme(
            text = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 24),          # to increased size
            axis.text.y = element_text(size = 32, face="bold"),                         # to increased size y-axis text
            # Inset shares the main panel's x scale, so its own tick labels are dropped
            axis.text.x = element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
            legend.position = "none",
            panel.grid = element_blank(),
            plot.title = element_blank(),
            axis.title = element_blank(),
            panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 1.5)  # to increased size border
          )
      ),
      # Start just past the longest main-plot bar in the inset's rows (ranks 5-135 from the
      # bottom), so the inset never covers a bar
      xmin = sort(data_plt$Importance)[135] * 1.05,
      xmax = (quantile(data_plt$Importance, 1) - quantile(data_plt$Importance, 0.5)) * .9 + quantile(data_plt$Importance, 0.5),
      ymin = 5,
      ymax = 135
    )
}
```

# Figure 6 (Permutation Test)

```{r}
# The permutation-test objects are not created anywhere in this notebook, so they must
# be loaded. IMPORTANT: `results` below is the permutation LIST (one data.frame per DDM
# parameter, with Category / P_Value columns) -- NOT the regression `results` data.frame
# built in DDM_STDDM_Regression.Rmd. If that one is in the session it shadows this, and
# results[[<measure>]] silently returns NULL ('argument is of length zero').
#
# permutation_test_test_level.RData  -> 12 OVERARCHING categories (published Figure 6)
# permutation_test_factor_level.RData -> 43 sub-categories (BIG5 - Extraversion, ...)
# Both store the object under the name final_factor_results.
perm_env <- new.env()
load('permutation_test_test_level.RData', envir = perm_env)
perm_results         <- perm_env$final_factor_results
final_factor_results <- perm_env$final_factor_results
final_results        <- perm_env$final_factor_results

# Loop through each category in results and filter significant p-values
significant_results <- list()
measures <- c("time", "b_gain", "b_risk", "alpha", "theta", "bias")
for (category in measures) {
  df <- perm_results[[category]]  # Extract dataframe for the category
  
  # Filter rows where P_Value is significant
  sig_df <- df[df$P_Value > 0.95 | df$P_Value < 0.05, ]
  
  # If significant results exist, store them
  if (nrow(sig_df) > 0) {
    significant_results[[category]] <- sig_df[, c("Category", "P_Value")]
  }
}
```


```{r}
# Run a FDR test

# Load necessary package
library(dplyr)

# Function to compute FDR corrected p-values
compute_fdr_p_values <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      FDR_P_Value = p.adjust(P_Value, method = "fdr"),  # Standard FDR correction
      Flipped_P_Value = 1 - P_Value,  # Flip the probabilities
      FDR_Flipped_P_Value = p.adjust(Flipped_P_Value, method = "fdr") # Apply BH correction to flipped values
    ) 
  return(df)
}

# Apply the function to each category in results
final_factor_results <- lapply(final_factor_results, compute_fdr_p_values)

```


```{r}
# Create plots for each measure
measures <- c("time", "b_gain", "b_risk", "alpha", "theta", "bias")
measure_labels <- c(
  "time" = "Time",
  "b_gain" = "Cure Sensitivity",
  "b_risk" = "Harm Sensitivity",
  "alpha" = "Response Caution",
  "theta" = "Non-Decision Time",
  "bias" = "Bias"
)

library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

# Define function to create and save plots
plot_permutation_test <- function(category_name, df) {
# Convert Null_Distribution into long format for boxplot
  null_dist_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:nrow(df), function(i) {
    data.frame(Category = df$Category[i], Value = as.numeric(unlist(df$Null_Distribution[i])))
  }))
  
  # Identify categories with p-value > 0.95
  df$Significance <- ifelse(df$P_Value > 0.95, "***", "")
  
  # Extract test means
  test_means <- data.frame(Category = df$Category, Value = df$test_mean, Error = df$test_sd, Significance = df$Significance)

  # Get the new title
  title_name <- measure_labels[[category_name]]
  
  # Generate plot
  p <- ggplot(null_dist_long, aes(x = Category, y = Value)) +
    geom_violin(fill = "lightblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +  
    # Individual null distribution points (small, transparent blue)
    # geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3, color = "blue", size = 1) +
    # Test mean as a red dot
    geom_point(data = test_means, aes(x = Category, y = Value), color = "red", size = 3) + 
    # Add error bars around the test means
    geom_errorbar(data = test_means, aes(x = Category, ymin = Value - Error, ymax = Value + Error), 
                  width = 0.2, color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
    #     # Add asterisks for p-value > 0.95
    # geom_text(data = test_means, aes(x = Category, y = Value + Error + 0.02, label = Significance), 
    #           color = "black", size = 6, fontface = "bold") +
    # White background
    theme_classic(base_family = "arial") +  
    # Labels
    labs(title = paste0("Feature Importance for ", title_name), x = "Category", y = "Feature\nImportance") +
    # Styling
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 24),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 32, face = "bold"),  # Larger x-axis title
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 32, face = "bold"),  # Larger y-axis title
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 18),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "white"),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "white"),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 36, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 25)),  # Centered, larger title
      plot.margin = margin(10, 40, 40, 40),
      panel.spacing = unit(0.5, "lines")
    )

  # Save the figure
  output_path <- paste0("Figures/NewPermutationTest_", category_name, ".png")
  ggsave(output_path, p, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300, limitsize=FALSE)
}

# Loop through each category in results and create plots
for (category in measures) {
  plot_permutation_test(category, final_results[[category]])
}
```

## Combined Figure 5 (main text)

Harm sensitivity and time on top, non-decision time centered below; the legend is in the
caption. Stars come from the FDR-corrected permutation p-values (within each parameter,
corrected separately for higher- and lower-than-chance importance), so they always match the
results. The single panels above stay as the supplementary version with all six parameters.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# P_Value = share of the null distribution at or below the observed mean, so values near 1
# mean higher-than-chance importance and values near 0 lower-than-chance
add_fdr_stars <- function(df) {
  df$q_high <- p.adjust(1 - df$P_Value, method = "fdr")
  df$q_low  <- p.adjust(df$P_Value, method = "fdr")
  df$Significance <- ifelse(df$q_high < .05 | df$q_low < .05, "*", "")
  df
}

make_permutation_panel <- function(measure, df) {
  df <- add_fdr_stars(df)
  null_dist_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(df)), function(i) {
    data.frame(Category = df$Category[i], Value = as.numeric(unlist(df$Null_Distribution[i])))
  }))
  # Star sits just above the higher of the violin top and the error bar
  null_max <- tapply(null_dist_long$Value, null_dist_long$Category, max)
  df$star_y <- pmax(null_max[df$Category], df$test_mean + df$test_sd) * 1.08

  ggplot(null_dist_long, aes(x = Category, y = Value)) +
    geom_violin(fill = "lightblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_errorbar(data = df, aes(x = Category, y = test_mean,
                                 ymin = test_mean - test_sd, ymax = test_mean + test_sd),
                  width = 0.2, color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(data = df, aes(x = Category, y = test_mean), color = "red", size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = df, aes(x = Category, y = star_y, label = Significance),
              size = 20, fontface = "bold") +
    theme_classic(base_family = "Arial") +
    labs(title = measure_labels[[measure]], x = "Category", y = "Feature\nImportance") +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 36),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 32),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 44, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 44, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 25)),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 56, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.margin = margin(10, 40, 20, 40)
    )
}

fig5_measures <- c("b_risk", "time", "theta")
fig5_panels <- lapply(fig5_measures, function(m) make_permutation_panel(m, final_results[[m]]))

# Two panels on top, the third centered below at the same size. The bottom row is built
# on its own (spacer | panel | spacer, widths 1:2:1) so the panel takes exactly half the
# row like each top panel; a shared grid would also give it the gutter between columns.
fig5_top    <- fig5_panels[[1]] | fig5_panels[[2]]
fig5_bottom <- (plot_spacer() | fig5_panels[[3]] | plot_spacer()) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2, 1))
fig5_plot <- (fig5_top / fig5_bottom) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1))   # both rows the same height

ggsave("Figures/permutation_test_final.png", fig5_plot, width = 34, height = 24, dpi = 300)
ggsave("Figures/permutation_test_final.pdf", fig5_plot, width = 34, height = 24, device = cairo_pdf)
print(fig5_plot)

# Starred categories, for checking against the text
for (m in fig5_measures) {
  d <- add_fdr_stars(final_results[[m]])
  cat(sprintf("%-7s high: %s | low: %s\n", m,
              paste(d$Category[d$q_high < .05], collapse = ", "),
              paste(d$Category[d$q_low < .05], collapse = ", ")))
}
```

## Look at benefits first individuals
